findings.title: Dynamic imports in appStore are still evaluated eagerly at module load time
findings.body: In `packages/app-store/index.ts`, each entry in `appStore` is defined as `applecalendar: import("./applecalendar")` rather than a lazy factory function `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")`. Because the `import(...)` expressions are evaluated immediately when the `appStore` object literal is constructed, importing `@calcom/app-store` still triggers loading of all 28 app-store packages at startup/module initialization rather than on demand when a specific app is requested. To actually defer loading until an app is used, each property should be a function (or getter) returning the `import()` promise and callers should invoke it.

findings.title: Async `forEach` callback pushes `deleteEvent` promises into `apiDeletes` after `Promise.all` runs
findings.body: When cancelling all remaining bookings of a recurring event (lines 458-470), `.forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... const deletedEvent = await calendar?.deleteEvent(...); apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` is used. Because `forEach` does not await its async callback, execution immediately moves past the loop while `await getCalendar(credential)` is still pending. By the time `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` (line 652) or `await apiDeletes` (line 617) executes, `apiDeletes` does not contain the calendar deletion promises, so the handler returns before recurring calendar events are actually deleted (and in serverless environments, the background deletions may be terminated mid-flight). Additionally, `await calendar?.deleteEvent(...)` pushes the resolved result rather than the promise into `apiDeletes`.

findings.title: `try/catch` around `forEach(async ...)` will not catch errors or await calendar event deletion
findings.body: In `packages/app-store/vital/lib/reschedule.ts` (lines 124-139) and identically in `packages/app-store/wipemycalother/lib/reschedule.ts` (lines 124-139) and `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx` (lines 553-567), `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... await getCalendar(...); ... })` is used. `Array.prototype.forEach` ignores the promise returned by an `async` callback: the surrounding `try { ... } catch` block will not catch any rejections from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` (resulting in unhandled promise rejections instead of logging via `logger.error`), and `Reschedule` / `requestReschedule` will proceed to send emails and return before calendar and video deletions have been initiated or completed. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async (bookingRef) => ...))` instead.
